headline: Sensex ends 333 points higher as Nifty crosses 23,200 level
why: Government cut windfall tax on the export of petrol, diesel, and ATF.
Benchmark indices snapped a two-day losing streak driven by bargain hunting.
Robust primary market activity provided underlying support to overall sentiment.
whatHappening: Retail investors shifted focus to IPOs, selling Rs 5,674 crore in the secondary market.
US Fed raised interest rates and signaled another potential hike later in 2026.
Shriram Finance announced plans to initiate a $500 million bond buyback.
Short-dated US Treasury yields spiked in reaction to the Fed's hawkish stance.

summary:
Indian benchmark indices snapped a two-day decline as Sensex rose 333 points and Nifty reclaimed 23,200.
Positive domestic triggers like windfall tax cuts offset global pressure from US Federal Reserve rate hikes.
